# Draft:Howard Roy Elseth

Howard Roy Elseth (also credited as H. Roy Elseth or Howard R. Elseth) is an American Christian author known for his 1977 book Did God Know? A Study of the Nature of God, which discusses divine foreknowledge and has been cited in discussions of open theism.Elseth's 1977 book Did God Know? A Study of the Nature of God explores God’s omniscience, human freedom, and moral responsibility; it includes a frequently quoted analogy about parental foreknowledge and culpability in discussions of open theism. He is also associated with the 1611 King James Bible Museum.
Elseth authored Did God Know? (Calvary United Church, 1977), which includes an analogy on parental foreknowledge and responsibility often referenced in open theism literature.
In 2009 he published 1611 Encrypted in the Holy Bible with Infinity Publishing, reflecting his interest in the history and reception of the King James Bible.
(Note: Independent secondary sources on Elseth are limited; the article relies primarily on primary materials.)
